add.after: …We will send someone.

quote.hanja: 上欲自將大軍繼之；癸巳，皇后抗表諫親征高麗；詔從之。
quote.ko: 황제는 몸소 대군을 이끌고 뒤따르려 하였다. 계사일, 황후가 표를 올려 고구려 친정을 간하니, 조서를 내려 그 말을 따랐다.
quote.html: The emperor meant to lead the great army after them himself. On the guisi day the Empress sent up a memorial against a personal campaign in Goguryeo, and an edict followed her advice.
quote.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 200, Tang Gaozong, Longshuo 1 (661), fourth month

add.why: The Tang court's own dry note on the beat the scene dramatizes (the Third Emperor wants to go, the Empress stops him). Placed after his '…We will send someone.' so the record confirms the outcome the scene just showed. Tang voice; the rest of this episode is seen from Goguryeo and Silla.

add.after: the White Dragon walks his army across the ice

quote.hanja: 契苾何力至，値氷大合，何力引衆乘氷渡水，鼓噪而進，我軍潰奔。何力追數十里，殺三萬人。餘衆悉降，男生僅以身免。
quote.ko: 계필하력이 이르렀을 때 마침 강물이 꽁꽁 얼어붙었다. 하력은 군사를 이끌고 얼음을 타고 강을 건너 북 치고 함성을 지르며 나아가니, 우리 군사가 무너져 달아났다. 하력은 수십 리를 쫓아가 삼만 명을 죽였다. 남은 무리는 모두 항복하고, 남생은 겨우 몸만 빠져나왔다.
quote.html: When the White Dragon arrived, the river had frozen solid. He led his men across on the ice, drumming and shouting as they came, and our army broke and ran. He pursued for dozens of li and killed thirty thousand. The rest all surrendered; Namseng barely got away with his life.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 22, Goguryeo Annals — King Bojang, yr. 20 (661), ninth month

add.why: Cross-nation pair, Goguryeo side. The Goguryeo annal says 我軍, 'our army', broke and ran. The next card is the same morning from the Tang side, where the same men are 賊, 'the bandits'. Insert after the ice-crossing paragraph and before Gesomun's 'One river, Namseng'. Namseng escaping is not a spoiler, since the next block has his father scolding him.

add.after: the White Dragon walks his army across the ice

quote.hanja: 次鴨綠水，蓋蘇文遣男生以精兵數萬拒險，眾莫敢濟。會冰合，何力引兵噪而濟，賊驚，遂潰。斬首三萬級，余眾降，男生脫身走。
quote.ko: 압록수에 이르니, 개소문이 남생에게 정병 수만을 주어 험한 곳을 막게 하여 아무도 감히 건너지 못하였다. 마침 얼음이 얼어붙자 하력이 군사를 이끌고 함성을 지르며 건너니, 적이 놀라 마침내 무너졌다. 삼만 급을 베고 남은 무리는 항복하였으며, 남생은 몸을 빼어 달아났다.
quote.html: He reached the Yalu. Gaesomun had sent Namseng with tens of thousands of picked troops to hold the crossing, and no one dared ford it. Then the ice closed. Heli led his men over with a roar; the bandits panicked and broke. Thirty thousand heads were taken and the rest surrendered. Namseng slipped away.
quote.source: Xin Tangshu (新唐書) bk. 110, Biography of Qibi Heli (契苾何力), Longshuo 1 (661)

add.why: Cross-nation pair, Tang side (same event id, insert directly after the Samguk Sagi card). Same numbers, opposite pronouns. If two cards in a 15-block episode is too many, keep only this one, because the narration already follows the Goguryeo telling closely.

add.after: The island kingdom sends its envoys to Silla and the Tang

quote.hanja: 耽羅國主佐平徒冬音律〈一作津。〉來降。耽羅自武德以來，臣屬百濟，故以佐平爲官號，至是，降爲屬國。
quote.ko: 탐라국주 좌평 도동음률〈진이라고도 한다〉이 와서 항복하였다. 탐라는 무덕 연간 이래 백제의 신하였으므로 좌평을 관호로 삼았는데, 이때에 이르러 항복하여 속국이 되었다.
quote.html: Dodongeumnyul (some copies say -jin), lord of Tamla and a jwapyeong, came and surrendered. Tamla had been Baekje's vassal since the Wude years, which is why its lord carried the Baekje rank of jwapyeong. Now it submitted and became a dependency.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 2 (662), second month

add.why: Silla's record of the island changing sides. Its lord still carries a Baekje rank title, which is a nice small irony. Note that the record says Tamla had served Baekje 'since Wude' (618), while the narration says 'seven centuries beside Baekje'. That is a contradiction to keep or smooth.

add.after: The island kingdom sends its envoys to Silla and the Tang

quote.hanja: 龍朔初，有儋羅者，其王儒李都羅遣使入朝，國居新羅武州南島上，俗樸陋，衣大豕皮，夏居革屋，冬窟室。…初附百濟。…後附新羅。
quote.ko: 용삭 초에 담라라는 나라가 있어, 그 왕 유리도라가 사신을 보내 입조하였다. 나라는 신라 무주 남쪽 섬 위에 있으며, 풍속이 소박하고 거칠어 큰 돼지 가죽을 입고, 여름에는 가죽 집에, 겨울에는 움집에 산다. … 처음에는 백제에 붙었다. … 뒤에는 신라에 붙었다.
quote.html: Early in Longshuo there was a land called Danluo, whose king, Yuri Dora, sent envoys to court. It lies on an island south of Silla's Muju. Its ways are plain and rough: they wear the hides of great pigs, live in leather huts in summer and in pit-houses in winter. … At first it was attached to Baekje. … Later it attached itself to Silla.
quote.source: Xin Tangshu (新唐書) bk. 220, Eastern Barbarians — Danluo (儋羅, Tamla), Longshuo era (661–663)

add.why: The Tang half of 'envoys to Silla and the Tang'. Same event id, insert right after the Silla card. The two records give the island two different kings (徒冬音律 / 儒李都羅) and the same switch of sides. I cut the 麟德中 sentence (the Taishan trip of 665) because it is later and not in the story.

add.after: Jinju and Jinheum are beheaded, and their households with them

quote.hanja: 八月，百濟殘賊，屯聚内斯只城作惡，遣欽純等十九將軍，討破之。大幢摠管眞珠、南川州摠管眞欽，詐稱病，閑放不恤國事，遂誅之，并夷其族。
quote.ko: 8월, 백제의 잔적이 내사지성에 모여 악행을 저지르니, 흠순 등 열아홉 장군을 보내 쳐서 깨뜨렸다. 대당총관 진주와 남천주총관 진흠이 병을 핑계 대고 한가로이 지내며 나랏일을 돌보지 않으므로, 마침내 그들을 베고 그 일족까지 멸하였다.
quote.html: In the eighth month the remnant rebels of Baekje gathered at Naesaji Fortress and did harm. Heumsun and the others, nineteen generals in all, were sent and broke them. Jinju, commander of the Great Banner, and Jinheum, commander of Namcheon, had pleaded illness and idled at their ease, careless of the kingdom's business. In the end they were put to death and their clans wiped out with them.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 2 (662), eighth month

add.why: The episode's whole incident in two sentences of annal: the 'two lines' Heumsun sends the king, made real. Placed after the execution paragraph so it confirms what was shown and does not announce it.

add.after: Eight years later, the same pages send a Jinju to behead a traitor governor

quote.hanja: 漢城州摠管藪世取百濟…國，適彼事覺，遣大阿飡眞珠，誅之。
quote.ko: 한성주총관 수세가 백제의 … 나라를 취하려 하다가 마침 그 일이 드러나니, 대아찬 진주를 보내 그를 베었다.
quote.html: Suse, commander of Hanseong-ju, took … of Baekje …; it happened that the plot came to light, and the daeachan Jinju was sent to put him to death.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 10 (670), twelfth month (the woodblock is damaged here)

add.why: This is the narrator's joke as evidence: the same annal kills Jinju in yr. 2 and sends him to execute someone in yr. 10. The '…' replaces six characters the woodblock lost (■■■■■■ in the edition). This one is optional; drop it if two cards are too many for a 14-block episode.

add.after: Namseng goes north to the old capital at Gungnae

quote.hanja: 男生懼不敢入。男建殺其子獻忠，男生走保國內城，率其衆與契丹、靺鞨兵附唐，遣子獻誠訴之。
quote.ko: 남생은 두려워 감히 들어가지 못하였다. 남건은 남생의 아들 헌충을 죽였다. 남생은 국내성으로 달아나 지키며, 제 무리와 거란·말갈 병사를 거느리고 당에 붙어, 아들 헌성을 보내 하소연하게 하였다.
quote.html: Namseng was afraid and dared not go in. Namgun killed Namseng's son Heonchung. Namseng fled to hold Gungnae Fortress, went over to Tang with his followers and his Khitan and Mohe troops, and sent his son Heonseong to plead his case.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 49, Biographies — Yeon Gaesomun (with Namseng)

add.why: Testimony 1 of 2, and effectively 3. SS bk. 49 copies Xin Tangshu bk. 110's 泉男生傳 almost word for word (I fetched both), so this card stands for both the Korean annal and the Tang court's version. It contradicts the scene, which is deliberate: here Namseng never comes to the gate ('dared not go in'), while the story has him under the wall calling Namgun a traitor. I cut the earlier sentences (rumours both ways, the spy caught, the forged summons), because blocks 4–7 already dramatize them almost line for line. The murdered son is not in the story, but he is no one's later reveal.

add.after: Namseng goes north to the old capital at Gungnae

quote.hanja: 公情思內款，事乖中執。方欲出撫邊甿，外巡荒甸，按嵎夷之舊壤，請羲仲之新官。二弟產建，一朝兇悖，能忍無親，稱兵內拒。金環幼子，忽就鯨鯢，玉膳長筵，俄辭顧復。
quote.ko: 공은 속마음으로 정성을 다했으나, 일은 조정 한가운데서 어그러졌다. 공이 막 변방 백성을 어루만지고 거친 들을 순시하러 나가, 동쪽 옛 땅을 살피고 새 관원을 청하려 할 때였다. 두 아우 남산과 남건이 하루아침에 흉악하게 패역하여, 혈육도 아랑곳없이 군사를 일으켜 안에서 막아섰다. 금고리를 찬 어린 아들은 졸지에 고래 아가리에 떨어져, 진수성찬 차린 긴 자리와 부모의 품을 문득 떠났다.
quote.html: His heart was loyal, but matters went wrong at the centre. He had just gone out to comfort the border folk and tour the wild marches, to survey the old lands of the dawn country and ask for new officers to govern them. Then his two younger brothers, Namsan and Namgun, turned vicious and rebellious in a single morning. Heartless to their own blood, they raised troops and shut him out from within. His little son with the gold ring fell suddenly into the whale's jaws, and left the long table and his parents' arms for ever.
quote.source: Epitaph of Yeon Namseng (泉男生墓誌) — Luoyang, 679; transcription in the Korean Ancient History DB (한국 고대 사료 DB)

add.why: Testimony 2: Namseng's own side, carved on his tomb in Luoyang. There is no spy and no rumour here. The brothers simply 'turned vicious in a single morning' while he was out on tour. It agrees with the annal on one thing, the murdered boy. Same event id; insert right after the Samguk Sagi card. Characters are verbatim from the DB 표점문; I swapped its western commas for 、，。 house punctuation. Optional: move both cards after the gate scene, after the line 'They say the taller a man stands, the longer his shadow.', if you'd rather they land on the confrontation than on the flight.

add.after: He puts a royal cousin, Anseung, under it.

quote.hanja: 高句麗水臨城人牟岑大兄，收合殘民，自窮牟城，至浿江南，殺唐官人及僧法安等。向新羅行，至西海史冶島，見高句麗大臣淵淨土之子安勝，迎致漢城中，奉以爲君。
quote.ko: 고구려 수림성 사람 대형 모잠이 남은 백성을 거두어 모아, 궁모성에서 패강 남쪽에 이르러 당의 관인과 승려 법안 등을 죽였다. 신라로 향해 가다가 서해 사야도에 이르러, 고구려 대신 연정토의 아들 안승을 만나 한성 안으로 맞아들이고 임금으로 받들었다.
quote.html: Mojam, a daehyeong of Goguryeo from Surim Fortress, gathered the surviving people, marched from Gungmo Fortress to south of the Pae River, and killed the Tang officials and the monk Beop'an. Heading for Silla, he reached Saya Island in the western sea, found Anseung, son of the Goguryeo minister Yeon Jungto, brought him into Hanseong, and set him up as lord.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 10 (670), sixth month

add.why: Cross-nation pair on who Anseung was. Silla's annal makes him the son of Yeon Jungto, the uncle who took twelve cities to Silla in Brothers' Coup, and this deserves a look against the story's 'royal cousin'. Here it is Mojam who heads for Silla, while the scene has Anseung wanting to go. The Silla annal also says nothing about Mojam's murder; only the Tang and Goguryeo annals mention it. Placed before the quarrel, so it opens no box.

add.after: He puts a royal cousin, Anseung, under it.

quote.hanja: 大長鉗牟岑率衆反，立藏外孫安舜爲主。
quote.ko: 대장 겸모잠이 무리를 거느리고 반란을 일으켜, 장왕의 외손 안순을 세워 임금으로 삼았다.
quote.html: The great chief Geom Mojam led his people in revolt and set up An Shun, King Jang's grandson through a daughter, as their lord.
quote.source: Xin Tangshu (新唐書) bk. 220, Eastern Barbarians — Goguryeo, Zongzhang 2 / Xianheng 1 (669–670)

add.why: Tang side, same event id, insert after the Silla card. To the Tang he is the king's daughter's son, with a different character in his name (舜 for 勝). For the record, the Goguryeo annal, SS bk. 22, calls him 王之庶子, the king's son by a concubine. That makes three parentages for one man. I stopped before the next sentence, 舜殺鉗牟岑走新羅 ('Shun killed Mojam and fled to Silla'), so the card doesn't announce the murder two blocks early.

add.after: Good. Give him a seal. A big one.

quote.hanja: 新羅王致命高句麗嗣子安勝。…先王正嗣，唯公而已，主於祭祀，非公而誰？…就披策命公爲高句麗王，公宜撫集遺民，紹興舊緖，永爲鄰國，事同昆弟，敬哉敬哉。
quote.ko: 신라왕은 고구려의 대를 이을 아들 안승에게 명한다. … 선왕의 바른 후사는 오직 공뿐이니, 제사를 받들 이가 공이 아니면 누구이겠는가? … 이에 책서를 펴서 공을 고구려왕으로 봉하노니, 공은 남은 백성을 어루만져 모으고 옛 왕업을 이어 일으켜, 길이 이웃 나라가 되어 형제처럼 지낼지어다. 삼가고 삼갈지어다.
quote.html: The King of Silla charges Anseung, heir of Goguryeo. … The rightful heir of the former kings is you and no one else; who but you should keep their sacrifices? … We open this patent and name you King of Goguryeo. Gather the surviving people, revive the old line, be our neighbour for ever and deal with us as a brother. Be reverent, be reverent!
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 10 (670), eighth month — patent investing Anseung

add.why: The 'big seal' itself: Munmu's actual patent of investiture. It lands right after his line, as the useful fiction put in writing. It could also be rendered as a `letter` block (from munmu to Anseung, seal 新羅王印) if you'd like a second letter outside the Letters episode.

add.after: Turn back while there is still a road to turn on.

quote.hanja: 亦由持彈而往，暗於枯井之危，捕蟬而前，不知黄雀之難，此王之不知量也。…嗚呼，昔爲忠義，今乃逆臣，恨始吉而終凶，怨本同而末異。風高氣切，葉落年悲，憑山遠望，有傷懷抱。
quote.ko: 이는 탄궁을 들고 나서면서 마른 우물의 위험을 보지 못하고, 매미를 잡으려 나아가면서 뒤에서 노리는 꾀꼬리를 알지 못하는 것과 같으니, 이것이 왕께서 스스로를 헤아리지 못하시는 바입니다. … 아아, 예전에는 충의의 신하였는데 이제는 역신이 되셨습니다. 처음은 길하였으나 끝이 흉함이 한스럽고, 뿌리는 같았으나 끝이 갈라짐이 원망스럽습니다. 바람은 높고 기운은 매서우며, 잎이 지니 한 해가 서럽습니다. 산에 기대어 멀리 바라보니 가슴이 아픕니다.
quote.html: It is like a man who goes out with his sling and never sees the dry well at his feet, or reaches for the cicada and never knows the oriole is behind him. That is Your Majesty, not knowing your own measure. … Alas! Once loyal and righteous, now a rebel subject. I grieve that what began in good fortune ends in ill, that what grew from one root ends in different branches. The wind is high and the air is sharp; the leaves fall and the year turns sad. I lean on the mountain and look far off, and it wounds my heart.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), seventh month — Xue Rengui's letter, carried by the monk Imyun

add.why: THE FIRST LETTER. Place it after Xue's read-aloud dialogue, as the page itself. Block 3's dialogue already paraphrases three other parts of the letter closely: 'A clear wind blows ten thousand li… the sea three thousand' = 淸風萬里，大海三千; 'your own brother waits in Chang'an' = 兄爲逆首，弟作忠臣; 'Your father knelt… and was raised up' = 頓䫙天門…哀納先君. So I took two passages the dialogue does not touch: the cicada-and-oriole threat and the closing autumn lament. Nothing duplicated. The menace under the courtesy is very Xue.

add.after: My father made me learn those words when I was twenty-two.

quote.hanja: 先王貞觀二十二年，入朝，面奉太宗文皇帝恩勅。『朕今伐高麗，非有他故，憐伱新羅，攝乎兩國，毎被侵陵，靡有寧歳。山川土地，非我所貪，玉帛子女，是我所有。我平定兩國，平壤已南百濟土地、並乞伱新羅，永爲安逸。』
quote.ko: 선왕께서는 정관 22년에 입조하시어 태종 문황제의 은혜로운 칙명을 직접 받드셨습니다. ‘짐이 지금 고구려를 치는 것은 다른 까닭이 아니다. 너희 신라가 두 나라 사이에 끼여 늘 침략을 당하고 편한 해가 없음을 가엾이 여기기 때문이다. 산천과 토지는 내가 탐내는 바가 아니요, 옥백과 자녀는 나에게도 넉넉하다. 내가 두 나라를 평정하면 평양 이남과 백제 땅을 모두 너희 신라에 주어, 길이 편안하게 하리라.’
quote.html: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan my late father went to court and received, face to face, the gracious edict of the Second Emperor: ‘We make war on Goguryeo now for no other reason than pity for you, Silla, caught between two kingdoms, invaded again and again, never a year of peace. Mountains, rivers and land are not what We covet; jade, silk, sons and daughters We have already. When We have pacified the two kingdoms, the land south of Pyongyang and the land of Baekje shall all be given to you, Silla, to rest in for ever.’
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), seventh month — King Munmu's reply to Xue Rengui

add.why: THE REPLY, part 1: the promise. HEADS-UP: block 13's first dialogue line closely paraphrases the key clause ('everything south of Pyongyang, and the whole of Baekje, shall be Silla's, forever'). The card adds the full edict, including the line 'mountains and rivers are not what We covet'. Decide whether to trim the dialogue line or keep both. Keeping both turns the card into the payoff of the plant in Mount Gain, where Munmu says 'My father made me learn it by heart.'

add.after: We were late, he said. We are always late. We came anyway.

quote.hanja: 南運熊津，北供平壤，蕞小新羅，分供兩所，人力疲極，牛馬死盡。…新羅百姓，草根猶自不足，熊津漢兵，粮食有餘。…一萬漢兵，四年衣食新羅，仁願已下，兵士已上，皮骨雖生漢地，血肉倶是新羅。
quote.ko: 남으로는 웅진에 실어 나르고 북으로는 평양에 대느라, 작은 신라가 두 곳을 나누어 감당하니 사람의 힘은 다하고 소와 말은 모두 죽었습니다. … 신라 백성은 풀뿌리조차 모자랐는데, 웅진의 당병은 양식이 남아돌았습니다. … 당병 1만이 4년 동안 신라에서 입고 먹었으니, 인원부터 졸병에 이르기까지 가죽과 뼈는 비록 당나라 땅에서 났으나, 피와 살은 모두 신라의 것입니다.
quote.html: South we carried grain to Bear Ford, north we fed Pyongyang; little Silla supplied two places at once, until our people were spent and our oxen and horses dead. … The people of Silla had not even enough grass roots to eat, while the Han soldiers at Bear Ford had grain to spare. … Ten thousand Han soldiers were clothed and fed by Silla for four years. From Liu Renyuan down to the last private, their skin and bones may have been born in Han land, but their blood and flesh are all Silla's.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), seventh month — King Munmu's reply to Xue Rengui

add.why: THE REPLY, part 2: the rice. The dialogue tells Yushin's snow march, and the letter gives the ledger behind it, so nothing is duplicated. 'Skin and bones Han, blood and flesh Silla' is the letter's most quoted line. White River no longer quotes this letter (the 倭船千艘 excerpt is gone from the current file), so there is no overlap.

add.after: I shelter the people your officials could not be bothered to count.

quote.hanja: 嗚呼。兩國未定平，蒙指蹤之驅馳，野獸今盡，反見烹宰之侵逼。賊殘百濟，反蒙雍齒之賞，殉漢新羅，已見丁公之誅。大陽之曜，雖不廻光，葵藿本心，猶懷向日。
quote.ko: 아아! 두 나라가 아직 평정되지 않았을 때는 손짓 하나에 사냥개처럼 내달렸는데, 들짐승이 다하자 도리어 삶아 죽이려는 핍박을 받습니다. 적의 찌꺼기인 백제는 도리어 원수에게 내리는 상을 받고, 한나라를 위해 목숨 바친 신라는 벌써 은인에게 내리는 칼을 받습니다. 태양의 빛이 비록 이쪽으로 돌아 비추지 않더라도, 해바라기의 본심은 여전히 해를 향합니다.
quote.html: Alas! While the two kingdoms stood, we were the hounds that ran at your pointing finger. Now the game is all taken, and it is we who are threatened with the pot. Baekje, the bandits' leavings, is rewarded the way Han once paid off an old enemy; Silla, which died for Han, is cut down the way Han once killed a man for sparing it. Though the sun's light no longer turns our way, the sunflower's heart still faces the sun.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), seventh month — King Munmu's reply to Xue Rengui

add.why: THE REPLY, part 3: the climax. Hounds cooked when the hunt is over, then the sunflower that still faces the sun. Its anger matches the dialogue's 'You say I shelter rebels', but nothing overlaps. 雍齒 (Yong Chi) and 丁公 (Lord Ding) are glossed in the English rather than named, to keep the name budget. Place it after block 16, before the sign-off line 'My brother is in Chang'an'.

add.after: a Silla squadron finds seventy Tang transports riding low

quote.hanja: 冬十月六日，撃唐漕船七十餘艘，捉郞將鉗耳大侯、士卒百餘人。其淪沒死者，不可勝數。級飡當千功第一，授位沙飡。
quote.ko: 겨울 10월 6일, 당의 조운선 70여 척을 쳐서 낭장 겸이대후와 사졸 백여 명을 사로잡았다. 물에 빠져 죽은 자는 이루 셀 수 없었다. 급찬 당천의 공이 으뜸이어서 사찬의 관등을 주었다.
quote.html: Winter, the sixth day of the tenth month: we struck more than seventy Tang grain transports and captured the colonel Qianer Dahou and over a hundred soldiers. The drowned were past counting. The geupchan Dangcheon's merit was first, and he was raised to sachan.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), tenth month

add.why: SEVENTY SHIPS. A regular record card, not a letter, for the scene's payoff. Bonus plant: the 'one Tang colonel', Qianer Dahou (鉗耳大侯), is the prisoner Silla hands back with its apology in Stone Gate. That annal entry names him (所留兵船郞將鉗耳大侯), so the plant fires.

add.after: The Mohe cavalry come in on a Silla army that has not yet formed up

quote.hanja: 我兵與高句麗兵逆戰，斬首數千級。高侃等退，追至石門戰之，我兵敗績，大阿飡曉川、沙飡義文、山世…等死之。
quote.ko: 우리 군사가 고구려 군사와 함께 맞받아 싸워 수천 급을 베었다. 고간 등이 물러나자 석문까지 뒤쫓아 싸웠는데, 우리 군사가 크게 패하여 대아찬 효천, 사찬 의문·산세 … 등이 전사하였다.
quote.html: Our troops and the Goguryeo troops met the enemy and took several thousand heads. When Gao Kan and the rest fell back, we chased them as far as Seokmun and fought there, and our army was routed. The daeachan Hyocheon, the sachan Uimun and Sanse … and others died there.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 12 (672), eighth month

add.why: Cross-nation pair, Silla side: a win, then the chase, then the rout, exactly as the narration has it. The '…' drops four more officers' names to keep the name budget.

add.after: The Mohe cavalry come in on a Silla army that has not yet formed up

quote.hanja: 十二月，高侃與高麗餘眾戰於白水山，破之。新羅遣兵救高麗，侃擊破之。
quote.ko: 12월, 고간이 고구려의 남은 무리와 백수산에서 싸워 깨뜨렸다. 신라가 군사를 보내 고구려를 구원하자, 고간이 그마저 쳐서 깨뜨렸다.
quote.html: Twelfth month: Gao Kan fought the Goguryeo remnants at Mount Baeksu and broke them. Silla sent troops to rescue Goguryeo, and Gao Kan broke those too.
quote.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 202, Tang Gaozong, Xianheng 3 (672), twelfth month

add.why: Tang side, same event id, insert directly after the Silla card. The Tang remembers two clean victories, dates them four months later, and never mentions Silla's first win or the gate.

add.after: and hands back the prisoners

quote.hanja: 臣某死罪謹言…南山之竹，不足書臣之罪，褒斜之林，未足作臣之械。瀦池宗社，屠裂臣身，事聽勅裁，甘心受戮。
quote.ko: 신 아무개는 죽을죄를 지었기에 삼가 아룁니다. … 남산의 대나무를 다 써도 신의 죄를 적기에 모자라고, 포야의 숲을 다 베어도 신의 형틀을 만들기에 모자랍니다. 종묘사직을 허물어 못으로 만들고 신의 몸을 찢어 죽이시더라도, 모든 일은 칙명의 처분을 따를 것이니 달게 죽음을 받겠습니다.
quote.html: Your servant, guilty unto death, respectfully reports. … All the bamboo of the Southern Mountain would not be enough to write down your servant's crimes, nor all the forests of Baoxie to make his shackles. Flood our ancestral temple, tear your servant limb from limb: in this I await the imperial decision, and accept execution with a willing heart.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 12 (672), ninth month — memorial of apology to the Tang court

add.why: The apology itself, in Munmu's own grovelling hand. A year after 'nowhere in it is the word sorry', it is all sorry, and the reader can enjoy how little he means it. The same annal entry lists the returned prisoners, including the colonel taken with the seventy ships (see Letters). This could also be rendered as a `letter` block (from munmu to gaozong, seal 新羅王印).

add.after: is told to die there and does not

quote.hanja: 庾信子元述，為裨將，亦欲戰死，其佐淡凌，止之曰：「大丈夫，非死之難，處死之為難也。若死而無成，不若生而圖後效。」…淡凌攬轡不放，遂不能死。
quote.ko: 유신의 아들 원술은 비장으로서 그 역시 싸우다 죽으려 하였다. 그를 보좌하던 담릉이 말리며 말하였다. “대장부는 죽는 것이 어려운 것이 아니라, 죽을 자리를 가리는 것이 어려운 법입니다. 죽어도 이루는 것이 없다면, 살아서 뒷날의 공을 도모하느니만 못합니다.” … 담릉이 고삐를 붙들고 놓지 않으니, 마침내 죽지 못하였다.
quote.html: Yushin's son Wonsul, a lieutenant, also meant to die fighting. His aide Danneung stopped him: “For a true man, dying is not the hard part. Choosing where to die is. If you die and achieve nothing, better to live and earn it later.” … Danneung held the bridle and would not let go, and so he could not die.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 43, Biographies — Kim Yushin, part 3 (Wonsul, 672)

add.why: The scene says Wonsul 'is told to die there and does not' but never shows who held him back. This card does, with a man holding a bridle. I left out Yushin's 元述不惟辱王命，而亦負家訓，可斬也 on purpose, because block 1's dialogue ('He shamed the king's command and the family name') already paraphrases it closely. I also cut Wonsul's reply 男兒不苟生… because the edition's text there reads '答田曰', which is garbled.

add.after: not Sacred Bone, not True Bone

quote.hanja: 王以丸都城經亂，不可復都，築平壤城，移民及廟社。平壤者本仙人王儉之宅也。或云王之都王儉。
quote.ko: 왕은 환도성이 난리를 겪어 다시 도읍으로 삼을 수 없으므로, 평양성을 쌓고 백성과 종묘사직을 옮겼다. 평양은 본래 선인 왕검이 살던 곳이다. 혹은 왕의 도읍인 왕검이라고도 한다.
quote.html: Because Hwando Fortress had been ravaged and could not serve as capital again, the king built Pyongyang Fortress and moved the people, the ancestral temple and the altars there. Pyongyang was originally the dwelling of the immortal Wanggeom. Some say it was the king's capital, Wanggeom.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 17, Goguryeo Annals — King Dongcheon, yr. 21 (247)

add.why: The one line in the Three Kingdoms' own annals that names Wanggeom as a person: 'the immortal Wanggeom', whose house Pyongyang was. It backs the stranger's title without explaining it, in keeping with the narrator's 'does not explain it'. No other nation records this, so there is no pair. Spoiler-safe.

add.after: Now the son is showing the enemy fleet the way into his own coast

quote.hanja: 秋九月，薛仁貴以宿衛學生風訓之父金眞珠，伏誅於本國，引風訓爲鄕導，來攻泉城。
quote.ko: 가을 9월, 설인귀는 숙위학생 풍훈의 아버지 김진주가 본국에서 처형된 일을 빌미로 삼아, 풍훈을 길잡이로 앞세우고 천성을 치러 왔다.
quote.html: Autumn, ninth month: since Kim Jinju, father of the palace-guard student Punghun, had been executed in his own country, Xue Rengui took Punghun as his guide and came to attack Cheonseong.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 15 (675), ninth month

add.why: This pays off the plant from Rebellion (Punghun: 'I can wait for a ship') and the teaser in The Wanggeom's Guest. I trimmed before 我將軍文訓等逆戰勝之，斬首一千四百級… so the card doesn't announce Munhun's ambush, which blocks 5–12 play out.

add.after: he has not paid that off yet

quote.hanja: 至乙亥年，唐兵來，攻買蘇川城，元述聞之，欲死之，以雪前恥，遂力戰有功賞，以不容於父母，憤恨不仕，以終其身。
quote.ko: 을해년에 이르러 당병이 와서 매소천성을 치자, 원술은 이를 듣고 거기서 죽어 지난날의 치욕을 씻고자 하였다. 마침내 힘껏 싸워 공을 세우고 상을 받았으나, 부모에게 끝내 용납받지 못한 것을 분하고 한스럽게 여겨, 벼슬하지 않고 생을 마쳤다.
quote.html: In the eulhae year the Tang army came and attacked Maesocheon Fortress. Wonsul heard of it and meant to die there, to wash away his old shame. He fought hard and earned merit and reward; but bitter that his parents had never taken him back, he would not hold office, and so ended his days.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 43, Biographies — Kim Yushin, part 3 (Wonsul at Maeso, 675)

add.why: The record behind block 21, where Wonsul leads the horse-cut and refuses rank. It closes the arc from the Wonsul episode. 'Ended his days' is not a spoiler, because no later episode shows Wonsul.

add.after: still, occasionally, checking his father

quote.hanja: 二十九日，李謹行率兵二十萬，屯買肖城，我軍撃走之，得戰馬三萬三百八十匹，其餘兵仗，稱是。
quote.ko: 29일, 이근행이 군사 20만을 거느리고 매소성에 주둔하였는데, 우리 군사가 쳐서 쫓아내고 전마 3만 380필을 얻었으며, 그 밖의 병장기도 그만큼 얻었다.
quote.html: On the twenty-ninth, Li Jinxing camped at Maeso Fortress with two hundred thousand men. Our army struck and drove him off, and took thirty thousand three hundred and eighty war-horses, with weapons and gear to match.
quote.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 15 (675), ninth month

add.why: Contradictory testimony, Silla side. It is placed after the 'Heads? / Horses, Majesty.' exchange and the paragraph that follows it (the 'Horses, Majesty.' line itself is too short to anchor on), so the card doesn't step on the punchline. The 30,380 is the number the courier just said.

add.after: still, occasionally, checking his father

quote.hanja: 詔以李謹行為安東鎮撫大使，屯新羅之買肖城以經略之，三戰皆捷，新羅乃遣使入貢，且謝罪；上赦之，復新羅王法敏官爵。
quote.ko: 조서를 내려 이근행을 안동진무대사로 삼아 신라의 매소성에 주둔하며 경략하게 하였다. 세 번 싸워 모두 이기니, 신라가 이에 사신을 보내 조공하고 또 사죄하였다. 황제는 이를 용서하고 신라왕 법민의 관작을 되돌려 주었다.
quote.html: By edict Li Jinxing was made Commissioner for Pacifying Andong and camped at Silla's Maeso Fortress to bring the country to order. He fought three battles and won them all. Silla then sent envoys with tribute and begged pardon; the emperor forgave it and restored King Bupmin of Silla to his titles.
quote.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 202, Tang Gaozong, Shangyuan 2 (675), second month

add.why: Tang side, same event id, insert right after the Silla card. It has the same fortress and the same general, but three Tang victories, dated to spring instead of autumn, and no horses at all. Xin Tangshu bk. 220 agrees with the Tang version (屯買肖城，三戰，虜皆北; also fetched). 'Bupmin' is the name the Tang used, which suits the Tang card.

add.after: Nobody there will need telling what the old country was called.

quote.hanja: 渤海靺鞨大祚榮者，本高麗別種也。高麗既滅，祚榮率家屬徙居營州。…祚榮遂率其衆東保桂婁之故地，據東牟山，築城以居之。
quote.ko: 발해말갈의 대조영은 본래 고구려의 별종이다. 고구려가 멸망하자 조영은 가솔을 거느리고 영주로 옮겨 살았다. … 조영은 마침내 무리를 이끌고 동쪽으로 가 계루의 옛 땅을 지키고, 동모산에 의지하여 성을 쌓고 살았다.
quote.html: Dae Joyoung of the Balhae Mohe was by origin a branch of the Goguryeo people. When Goguryeo was destroyed, Joyoung moved his household to Yingzhou. … At last he led his people east to hold the old land of the Gyeru, took Mount Dongmo, and built a walled town there to live in.
quote.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199B, Northern Di — the Balhae Mohe (渤海靺鞨)

add.why: Cross-nation pair on the episode's last idea: was Balhae Goguryeo? This is the Tang view: 'a branch of Goguryeo'. 桂婁, the Gyeru, was Goguryeo's royal clan, so 'the old land of the Gyeru' quietly answers the cave scene. Note the contradiction: the record has the family going west to Yingzhou before coming back east, while the story has them walking north.

add.after: Nobody there will need telling what the old country was called.

quote.hanja: 武藝啓。山河異域。國土不同。…武藝忝當列國。濫惣諸蕃。復高麗之舊居。有扶餘之遺俗。
quote.ko: 무예가 아룁니다. 산하는 지역이 다르고 국토는 같지 않습니다. … 무예는 황송하게도 열국의 하나를 맡아 외람되이 여러 번국을 거느리며, 고구려의 옛 터전을 되찾고 부여의 남은 풍속을 지니고 있습니다.
quote.html: Muye reports. Our mountains and rivers lie in other regions; our lands are not the same. … I, Muye, unworthily hold a place among the kingdoms and preside over the many tribes. We have restored the old home of Goguryeo, and we keep the customs handed down from Buyeo.
quote.source: Shoku Nihongi (續日本紀) bk. 10, Shōmu, Jinki 5 (728), first month — letter of Dae Muye, King of Balhae, to the Yamato court

add.why: Balhae answers for itself: Dae Joyoung's son writes to Yamato, 'We have restored the old home of Goguryeo.' Same event id; insert after the Jiu Tangshu card and before 'The Three Kingdoms Era is over.' It is the boy's own promise in the cave, kept in writing by his son. Punctuation is the edition's (。 throughout). Optional: render it as a `letter` block (from 'Dae Muye, King of Balhae' to 'the Yamato court', seal 渤海王印). The year 728 is after the story ends, but block 29 already says the kingdom will come, so it reveals nothing.

fix.match: he and his thirteen sons all died in battle
fix.after: He does not run. The arrows make a hedgehog of him
fix.why: SPOILER. The card sits third in the episode, right after the opening paragraph and the map, and announces that the White Tiger and all thirteen sons die before the count begins. Move it to right after his death paragraph ('He does not run. The arrows make a hedgehog of him…'), before Gesomun's 'White Tiger. / Titles drown too.' The text stays verbatim.

fix.match: took more than four thousand heads
fix.after: None of them are turning back.
fix.why: SPOILER. Right now the card says 'prevailed, and took more than four thousand heads' before the messenger arrives and Munmu asks 'Have we… won…?'. Move it to after the messenger's line 'They're heading west. None of them are turning back.', so the record confirms the news and Munmu's disbelief plays as dramatic irony. Alternative if you'd rather keep its position: trim to 沙飡施得領船兵 與薛仁貴戰於所夫里州伎伐浦 敗績 又進大小二十二戰… / '…fought twenty-two engagements great and small…' and cut 克之 斬首四千餘級 from hanja, ko and html.

notes: Scope: final-stand, silla-tang-war, epilogue-2, audited against the live story.json, which changed while I worked. A map block was inserted into Pyongyang I and Snake River, and White River lost most of its quotes, including the 倭船千艘 excerpt of Munmu's letter. All anchors are text fragments, so index shifts don't matter.
